transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… thank you, Doctor. I guess I’m here because things at work have gotten a bit difficult, and I’m trying to handle it appropriately.

I do environmental modeling contract work, and I’ve been noticing… patterns, I suppose, in the datasets and revisions. It seems like people on the contract are tracking my changes and maybe putting errors in, so it reflects badly on me—like I can’t lead the work. My wife and some of the junior analysts say it’s probably just version-control mistakes, and I’m trying to be fair about that, but it really doesn’t feel accidental to me.

Can you tell me more about your belief that people on the contract are deliberately sabotaging your work? Have you noticed any specific actions or evidence that supports this, or is it more of a feeling?

I mean… I don’t want to sound unreasonable, Doctor. I know there are normal version-control problems on projects like this. But it’s happened enough that it feels hard to dismiss.

I’ll make a set of revisions, and then later there’ll be errors in the dataset or the model inputs that I don’t remember putting there. And it seems to happen in places tied to my work, so if someone reviews it, it looks like I missed something basic. The junior analysts say it’s probably just file conflicts or accidental overwrites, and my wife has said maybe I’m reading too much into it… but I’m pretty sure someone on the contract is tracking what I change and planting those errors so it looks like I can’t lead the work.

I know that may sound strong. I’m just trying to explain it clearly.
Have you ever felt that people were trying to harm you or undermine your work before, or is this something new that's come up recently?

I don’t think it’s been a longstanding thing, no. At least, not like this.

I’ve had normal work frustrations before, like anyone, but this certainty that people on the project are tracking my revisions and putting errors in… that’s really been more recent. I’d say about the last two months. I know that may sound like a short time, or maybe I’m not describing it the right way, but that’s when it started feeling hard to explain as just mistakes.

Outside of your concerns at work, have you noticed any other unusual experiences, such as hearing things that others don’t hear, feeling like people are watching you when they aren’t, or feeling unusually down or hopeless?

I wouldn’t say anything dramatic like that, Doctor… at least, I don’t want to overstate it.

I guess outside of work I’ve been more… flat, maybe. These days I can sit for hours at my desk, or out in the garage with the telescope still covered, and I know I used to get a lot out of things like hiking, mentoring the younger analysts, going to astronomy nights. But I just don’t feel much pull to start any of it, or to talk to people.

It’s probably just stress, maybe. I’m not trying to make it sound worse than it is.
Have you ever felt that people are watching you, talking about you behind your back, or trying to control your thoughts or actions in any way?

Not control my thoughts, no… I don’t think I’d put it that way.

But watching what I’m doing at work, yes, in a sense. I’m pretty sure some people on the environmental modeling contract have been tracking my revisions and then planting errors in the datasets, so it looks like I can’t lead the work properly. I know my wife and a couple of the junior analysts keep saying it’s probably just version-control mistakes, and I understand why they’d say that… I just don’t think that explains all of it.

I hope that answers what you mean.
Have you ever felt that people outside of work were watching you, talking about you, or acting in a way that seemed personally targeted toward you?

Outside of work… no, not really in the same way. I don’t want to make it sound like I think everyone is after me or anything like that.

It’s more tied to that contract and the datasets. That’s where I keep seeing it — my revisions being tracked, errors showing up afterward, and it making me look like I can’t manage the project. My wife and the junior analysts keep saying it’s probably just version-control issues, and I hear that, I do… but it doesn’t feel like it explains what’s happening.

So, outside of work, I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed people targeting me like that.
Have you ever had any beliefs or concerns that others might consider unusual or unfounded, outside of this situation at work?

Outside of that work situation… I don’t think so, no. Not in any big way.

I mean, the main thing—the thing that brought me here—is that contract. I’m pretty sure people on that environmental modeling work have been tracking my revisions and then planting errors in the datasets, so it makes me look like I can’t lead it. I know that may sound… a little hard to prove, and my wife and the junior analysts keep saying it’s probably just version-control mistakes.

I understand why they’d say that. I’m not trying to be difficult. I just don’t think that explanation accounts for what I’m seeing. Outside of that, though, I can’t think of anything else unusual like that.
Have you ever had any beliefs that others might not share, even if they seemed obvious to you, outside of the concerns you've described at work?

I think… outside of work, no, not that I can think of. I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is.

The belief I have is really about that environmental modeling contract. It just seems obvious to me that my revisions were being followed and then errors were showing up in the datasets afterward, in a way that made me look like I couldn’t lead the work. I know my wife and the junior analysts don’t see it that way — they keep saying it’s probably version-control mistakes — and I understand that sounds more reasonable, maybe.

But to me, it doesn’t fully explain it. So… yes, others don’t really share that concern, but it’s mainly that one situation. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Can you tell me what you think might be going through the minds of the people you believe are tracking your revisions and planting errors?

I mean… I don’t want to make them sound evil or anything. That may be too strong.

But it feels like they think I’m in the way, maybe that I shouldn’t be leading the contract. Like if enough mistakes show up under my name, then it looks like I can’t manage the environmental modeling work properly. So when I see my revisions tracked and then errors appearing in the datasets afterward, it’s hard for me not to think there’s some intention behind it.

I know my wife and the junior analysts keep saying it could just be version-control problems, and I’m trying to be fair about that. I just… I don’t think that explains all of it. Does that make sense?
Do you think it's possible that others might not see the situation at work the same way you do, and that they might not believe someone is deliberately undermining your work?

Yes… I do think it’s possible they don’t see it the way I do. I mean, my wife definitely doesn’t. And the junior analysts keep saying it’s probably just version-control mistakes, not anyone trying to do anything on purpose.

I understand why that sounds more reasonable. I’m not trying to insist everyone has to agree with me. It’s just… from where I’m sitting, with the revisions being tracked and then errors showing up in the datasets afterward, it really does look like someone is trying to make it seem like I can’t lead the contract.

But yes, I know other people may not believe that. I can see that. I’m trying to be fair about it.
Even though others have said it’s likely version-control mistakes, do you feel absolutely certain that someone is deliberately tracking your revisions and planting errors, without any doubt?

I wouldn’t say “absolutely certain” in the sense that I can prove it in a courtroom or anything… I know that might sound too rigid.

But if I’m being honest, yes, I’m pretty sure that’s what’s happening. The pattern with my revisions being followed and then errors showing up in the datasets afterward just feels too specific to be ordinary version-control trouble.

I understand my wife and the junior analysts think I’m over-reading it, and I’m trying to leave room for that. I don’t want to seem unreasonable. But in my mind, it still really looks deliberate. Does that make sense?

Even though your wife and the junior analysts have suggested these are just version-control mistakes, do you still feel deep down that someone is intentionally following your work and placing errors in the datasets?

Yes… deep down, I do. I know that may not be the answer I’m supposed to give, and I’m trying not to sound paranoid or difficult.

But yes, I’m pretty sure someone on that environmental modeling contract is following my revisions and then putting errors into the datasets afterward, so it ends up looking like I can’t lead the work. I hear what my wife says, and what the junior analysts say about version-control mistakes… and I’m not dismissing them completely.

It’s just that, inside, it still feels intentional to me.

Even though there’s no direct evidence and others believe it’s version-control mistakes, do you still feel completely convinced that someone is intentionally tracking your work and inserting errors on purpose?

I… yes, I guess if I’m being honest, I do still feel convinced.

I know there isn’t direct evidence in the way you’re asking, and I know my wife and the junior analysts keep saying it’s probably just version-control mistakes. I don’t want to sound like I’m refusing to consider that.

But the reason I’m here is because I’m pretty sure the people on that environmental modeling contract have been tracking my revisions and then planting errors in the datasets, so it looks like I can’t lead the work. I realize how that sounds… but that’s still what it feels like to me.

Even though there is no clear proof and others have given alternative explanations, do you feel that your belief about being deliberately undermined at work is completely true and not something that could be a misunderstanding?

I… I want to say I’m leaving room for a misunderstanding, because I know that’s the reasonable answer, and I don’t want to sound like I’m being stubborn.

But if you’re asking what I really believe, then yes, I still think it’s true. I’m here because I’m pretty sure the people on that environmental modeling contract have been tracking my revisions and planting errors in the datasets so it looks like I can’t lead the work.

I know my wife and the junior analysts keep saying it’s probably version-control mistakes, and maybe I should be able to accept that more easily… but it doesn’t feel like a misunderstanding to me.
